what_matters.head: 34 of the 35 names rose on Monday; the S&P 500 fund gained 4.7%, about 4.3 × its usual day
what_matters.detail: Reuters says Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive drove investors back into AI-related shares after last week's rout. The S&P 500 rose 4.73% and the Nasdaq Composite 6.51%, their biggest daily percentage gains since April 2025, and the chip index rose 14% (Reuters). The S&P 500 recovered just over half of last week's loss (AP). Even so, 33 of the 34 names with a 50-day average are still below it. Anthropic was the only name that fell.

what_matters.head: Nvidia rose 31.5%, about 10.4 × its usual day, after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive
what_matters.detail: The board voted unanimously on Sunday 22 Nov to reinstate him as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately, and Nvidia announced it shortly before Monday's New York open. The release says the board 'received input from senior levels of the United States government' and 'is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk'. The independent directors' investigation 'will proceed to conclusion', and Colette Kress stays finance chief. President Trump told CNBC he had pressed the board to reinstate Huang (Reuters). Lawmakers of both parties criticised the decision. Huang testifies in public before the Senate Banking Committee on 3 Dec and is still expected at a closed-door interview with three House panels on 1 Dec (Reuters). It was Nvidia's biggest daily percentage gain since May 2003 (Reuters); the shares are still down 21.8% in a month.

what_matters.head: The US put Megaspeed, the Singapore-based former Nvidia customer, and six other Southeast Asian firms on its trade blacklist on Monday
what_matters.detail: The Commerce Department added them to the Entity List, the list of foreign companies that US suppliers need a licence to sell to; Reuters says approval is likely to be denied. One of the seven is Apex Enterprise Solutions, which Reuters calls Alibaba's Singapore subsidiary; Alibaba called the listing erroneous. IntelliNews says Nvidia put Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list in June 2025; how much revenue it earned through the firm before that is not disclosed. Malaysia's trade ministry said it will not allow itself to be used as a channel to circumvent export controls, and Singapore's prime minister said on Tuesday that its own Megaspeed investigation continues (Al Jazeera, Reuters). No notice was found in the Federal Register on Tuesday afternoon, Singapore time. Whether the listing came before or after Monday's US close is not clear from the reports.

latest.tape_note:
33 of the 34 names with a 50-day average are still below it, and more than half have been below in every report since 13 Oct. Three names have an RSI under 30, against 18 in the 6 Nov report.
The Nasdaq 100 fund rose 7.0%, about 4.1 × usual, and the chip fund 13.6%, about 3.8 × usual; Reuters ties both to investors returning to AI-related shares after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang. The chip fund is still down 12.0% in a month.
Gold rose 3.9%, about 2.3 × usual; Reuters says bargain hunters stepped in after last week's steep drop, and Bloomberg ties it to the wider rally after Huang's return (read through search results).
The 10-year yield rose 1bp to 4.92%.
The dollar index rose 0.5% to 104.32, its highest in the stored reports, which start on 12 March; Reuters says traders bet on a more hawkish Federal Reserve.
US crude fell 4.0% to 80.17, its lowest since the 10 Aug report; Reuters puts oil's fall down to an increase in Middle East supplies. The figure is on the new front-month contract.
Singapore's MAS core inflation eased to 1.5% in the year to October from 2.0% in September, and all-items inflation slowed to 1.9% from 2.2% (MAS, released Monday 23 Nov).
The high-yield credit spread was 3.76% on 20 Nov, the highest of its last seven monthly readings (low 2.63%). That reading is from before Monday's rally.

vix_note.text: The VIX measures how big a swing in the S&P 500 traders are paying to protect against over the next 30 days, worked out from options prices; it rises when stocks fall fast and more protection is bought. It closed at 26.62 on Monday, down 25.8% on the day, about 2.1 × its usual day, and still 36.9% higher than a month ago. Reuters' report on Monday's rally (item 1) says only that the index 'plunged'. No report found gives the VIX a cause of its own.
